'''Miguel Torres Gómez''' ({{IPA|es|miˈɣel ˈtores}}; born 28 January 1986) is a Spanish former professional [[Association football|footballer]]. Usually a [[right-back]], he was equally at ease on the other flank.<ref name=Valera>{{cite news|url=https://as.com/futbol/2011/10/19/mas_futbol/1319005656_850215.html|title=Torres: "Ya jugué de lateral izquierdo"|trans-title=Torres: "I've played as a left-back before"|newspaper=Diario AS|language=Spanish|date=19 October 2011|accessdate=31 January 2022}}</ref>

He appeared in 223 [[La Liga]] matches over 11 seasons, in representation of [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]], [[Getafe CF|Getafe]] and [[Málaga CF|Málaga]]. He also played in Greece with [[Olympiacos F.C.|Olympiacos]].

==Club career==
===Real Madrid===
Born in [[Madrid]], Torres joined [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]]'s junior teams at the age of 12. He made his first-team debut against [[Écija Balompié|Écija]] as a starter, in a [[Copa del Rey]] game on 25 October 2006, because of injuries to defenders [[Fabio Cannavaro]], [[Cicinho]] and [[Míchel Salgado]]. He also played in [[2006–07 Copa del Rey|the return leg]] as a [[Substitute (association football)|substitute]] after replacing [[Sergio Ramos]] in the 80th minute,<ref>{{cite news|url=http://futbol.as.com/futbol/2006/10/26/mas_futbol/1161844009_850215.html|title=Écija penetra en la galaxia|trans-title=Écija enters galaxy|newspaper=Diario AS|first=Juanma|last=Trueba|language=Spanish|date=26 October 2006|accessdate=10 August 2013}}</ref> and started in both cup matches against [[Real Betis]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://hemeroteca.mundodeportivo.com/preview/2007/01/12/pagina-14/861739/pdf.html|title=El Madrid apuesta por los jóvenes pero no ve puerta|trans-title=Madrid bet on youngsters but goal eludes them|newspaper=[[Mundo Deportivo]]|first=Jordi|last=Santamaría|language=Spanish|date=12 January 2007|accessdate=12 May 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=http://hemeroteca.mundodeportivo.com/preview/2007/01/19/pagina-10/1420772/pdf.html|title=Ridículo Madrid|trans-title=Ridiculous Madrid|newspaper=Mundo Deportivo|first=Andrés|last=Astruells|language=Spanish|date=19 January 2007|accessdate=12 May 2017}}</ref>

Torres made his [[La Liga]] debut in his fourth consecutive appearance, playing the whole 90 minutes in the 1–0 home victory over [[Real Zaragoza]] on 14 January 2007.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.elmundo.es/elmundodeporte/2007/01/14/futbol/1168803206.html|title=La tesis 'post-galáctica' da crédito a Capello|trans-title='Post-galactic' thesis gives credit to Capello|newspaper=[[El Mundo (Spain)|El Mundo]]|first=Fernando|last=Llamas|language=Spanish|date=14 January 2007|accessdate=12 May 2017}}</ref> He kept his place in the side the following week against [[RCD Mallorca|Mallorca]], with that performance leading coach [[Fabio Capello]] to state: "It is not easy to find a player with as much personality and talent in attack and defence as Torres".<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.elmundo.es/elmundodeporte/2007/01/22/futbol/1169420459.html|title=Capello: 'Hemos ganado con mérito'|trans-title=Capello: 'We deserved to win'|newspaper=El Mundo|language=Spanish|date=22 January 2007|accessdate=16 November 2018}}</ref>

On 10 February 2007, against [[Real Sociedad]], Torres made his first [[Assist (association football)|assist]]: after a quick run on the left flank he provided a [[Left-handedness|left-footed]] (he was right-footed by nature) cross for [[Ruud van Nistelrooy]], whose header found the net as Madrid came from behind to win it away 2–1.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://elpais.com/diario/2007/02/11/deportes/1171148402_850215.html|title=Regalo de Beckham a Capello|trans-title=Beckham offers one to Capello|newspaper=[[El País]]|first=Eduardo|last=Rodrigálvarez|language=Spanish|date=10 February 2007|accessdate=31 January 2022}}</ref>

With Torres as an important piece, Real Madrid [[2006–07 La Liga|won their 30th league title]]; however, he was unable to play in the decisive game with Mallorca due to a [[hamstring]] tear.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.elmundo.es/elmundodeporte/envivos/2007/06/5038_index.html|title=R. Madrid 3–1 Mallorca|newspaper=El Mundo|language=Spanish|date=17 June 2007|accessdate=16 November 2018}}</ref> He signed his first professional contract on 12 July 2007, joining the main squad permanently from [[Real Madrid Castilla]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://as.com/futbol/2007/07/13/mas_futbol/1184308046_850215.html?omnil=resrelart|title=Torres firmó su contrato profesional hasta 2012|trans-title=Torres signed his professional contract until 2012|newspaper=Diario AS|first=Daniel|last=García|language=Spanish|date=13 July 2007|accessdate=16 November 2018}}</ref>

Although Torres appeared in more league matches in the [[2007–08 La Liga|following season]], he would start significantly less as Madrid repeated league honours, primarily due to the signing of Argentine [[Gabriel Heinze]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.elconfidencial.com/deportes/2007-09-18/schuster-manda-a-saviola-a-la-grada_307209/|title=Schuster manda a Saviola a la grada|trans-title=Schuster sends Saviola to the stands|newspaper=[[El Confidencial]]|language=Spanish|date=18 September 2007|accessdate=16 November 2018}}</ref> During the [[2008–09 La Liga|2008–09 campaign]], still under [[Bernd Schuster]] first and later [[Juande Ramos]], he did not fare any better.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.larazon.es/historico/un-problema-mas-para-schuster-la-rodilla-derecha-ya-le-tuvo-un-ano-parado-KJLA_RAZON_50513|title=Un problema más para Schuster|trans-title=Another problem for Schuster|newspaper=[[La Razón (Madrid)|La Razón]]|language=Spanish|date=8 November 2008|accessdate=16 November 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.elmundo.es/elmundodeporte/2009/01/28/futbol/1233169974.html|title='De la Red pensaba que tenía más amigos'|trans-title='De la Red thought he had more friends'|newspaper=El Mundo|language=Spanish|date=28 January 2009|accessdate=16 November 2018}}</ref>

===Getafe===
On 31 August 2009 – [[Transfer window|transfer deadline day]] – Torres moved to neighbours [[Getafe CF|Getafe]] on a five-year contract, with Real having the option to rebuy in the first two.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.marca.com/2009/08/31/futbol/equipos/getafe/1251741764.html|title=Miguel Torres jugará en el Getafe las próximas cinco temporadas|trans-title=Miguel Torres will play in Getafe the next five seasons|newspaper=[[Marca (newspaper)|Marca]]|language=Spanish|date=31 August 2009|accessdate=31 August 2009}}</ref> He made 26 appearances in his [[2009–10 La Liga|first season]], with [[2010–11 UEFA Europa League|qualification]] to the [[UEFA Europa League]] after a sixth-place finish.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.marca.com/2010/05/15/futbol/equipos/getafe/1273957003.html|title=Míchel: "Es un día histórico"|trans-title=Míchel: "It's an historic day"|newspaper=Marca|language=Spanish|date=15 May 2010|accessdate=31 January 2022}}</ref>

Torres was challenged by new signing [[Juan Valera (footballer)|Juan Valera]] for the right-back position in the [[2011–12 La Liga|2011–12 season]], under new manager [[Luis García (footballer, born 1972)|Luis García]],<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.marca.com/2011/08/16/futbol/equipos/getafe/1313489566.html|title=Valera: "En el Getafe hay un proyecto ilusionante"|trans-title=Valera: "We have a hopeful project at Getafe"|newspaper=Marca|language=Spanish|date=16 August 2011|accessdate=31 January 2022}}</ref><ref name=Valera/> but still contributed 23 league matches as the [[Madrid]] outskirts team again retained their status. On 16 April 2012, he scored his only goal in the top division, opening a 5–1 home defeat of [[Sevilla FC|Sevilla]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report?id=323730&cc=5739|title=Five-goal Getafe crush Sevilla|publisher=[[ESPN FC|ESPN Soccernet]]|date=16 April 2012|accessdate=27 April 2012|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://archive.today/20120713201048/http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report?id=323730&cc=5739|archive-date=13 July 2012}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.marca.com/marcador/futbol/2011_12/primera/jornada_34/get_sev/|title=El show de Pedro Ríos|trans-title=The Pedro Ríos show|newspaper=Marca|first=Jaime|last=Rincón|language=Spanish|date=16 April 2012|accessdate=31 January 2022}}</ref>

===Olympiacos and Málaga===
On 9 August 2013, Torres joined [[Olympiacos F.C.|Olympiacos]] in Greece on a three-year deal worth a reported [[Euro|€]]500,000, reuniting with [[Míchel (footballer, born 1963)|Míchel]] who also coached him at Getafe and Real Madrid Castilla.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/025a-0ea8e7f2453f-cb0607d0fbee-1000--miguel-torres-joins-michel-at-olympiacos/|title=Miguel Torres joins Míchel at Olympiacos|publisher=UEFA|date=9 August 2013|access-date=26 August 2013}}</ref> After only ten competitive games, he returned to Spain's top flight a year later, signing a one-year contract at [[Málaga CF|Málaga]] with the option of two more.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.marca.com/2014/08/14/futbol/equipos/malaga/1408024440.html|title=Miguel Torres ya es jugador del Málaga|trans-title=Miguel Torres is already a Málaga player|newspaper=Marca|first=Jesús|last=Ballesteros|language=Spanish|date=14 August 2014|accessdate=19 November 2016|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161119183241/http://www.marca.com/2014/08/14/futbol/equipos/malaga/1408024440.html|archive-date=19 November 2016}}</ref>

During his later spell at the [[La Rosaleda Stadium]], Torres suffered several injury problems and was also deemed surplus to requirements by manager [[Juan Ramón López Muñiz]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.marca.com/futbol/malaga/2019/04/30/5cc85c56468aeb49358b45d8.html|title=El fin de la pesadilla y la nueva vida de Miguel Torres|trans-title=The end of the nightmare and Miguel Torres' new life|newspaper=Marca|first=César|last=Suárez|language=Spanish|date=30 April 2019|accessdate=23 July 2019}}</ref> On 4 July 2019, the 33-year-old announced his retirement from football.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.marca.com/futbol/malaga/2019/07/04/5d1e1b1546163f96bf8b458d.html|title=Miguel Torres dice adiós al fútbol|trans-title=Miguel Torres says goodbye to football|newspaper=Marca|first=Juanje|last=Fernández|language=Spanish|date=4 July 2019|accessdate=8 July 2019}}</ref>

==International career==
Torres made his debut for the [[Spain national under-21 football team|Spain under-21 team]] on 6 February 2007 in a 2–2 draw against [[England national under-21 football team|England]],<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2007/feb/07/newsstory.englandfootballteam|title=Lita arrives late and does his level best for Pearce's England|newspaper=[[The Guardian]]|first=Richard|last=Rae|date=7 February 2007|accessdate=11 April 2017}}</ref> remaining a regular in subsequent fixtures.

==Personal life==
[[File:25th Laureus World Sports Awards - Red Carpet - Paula Echevarría, Miguel Torres - 240422 190037.jpg|thumb|right|Torres and Echevarría in 2024]]
In 2021, Torres and actress [[Paula Echevarría]] became parents to a son, also named Miguel.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.lavanguardia.com/gente/20210820/7672815/primeras-vacaciones-miki-hijo-paula-echevarria-miguel-torres-mmn.html|title=Las primeras vacaciones de 'Miki', el hijo de Paula Echevarría y Miguel Torres|trans-title=The first holidays of 'Miki', the son of Paula Echevarría and Miguel Torres|newspaper=[[La Vanguardia]]|first=Eñaut|last=Zuazo|language=Spanish|date=20 August 2021|accessdate=22 August 2021}}</ref> The couple took part together on the [[Mask Singer: Adivina quién canta (season 3)|third season]] of ''[[Mask Singer: Adivina quién canta]]'', won by fellow Real Madrid veteran [[Fernando Morientes]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.marca.com/tiramillas/television/2023/07/06/64a6657ee2704e73bf8b45fd.html|title=Fernando Morientes y Ana Torroja sorprenden a todos y ganan la tercera edición de 'Mask Singer'|trans-title=Fernando Morientes and Ana Torroja surprise everyone and win the third edition of 'Mask Singer'|newspaper=Marca|language=Spanish|date=6 July 2023|accessdate=2 January 2024}}</ref>
